Before you drop by.

Do I need to be a Home Assistant expert?+

Nope. Brand-new users, long-time tinkerers, and people who are just curious are welcome. HomeKit, Google Home, and Alexa users too.

What should I bring to the meetup?+

Just yourself is plenty. Bring a phone or laptop if you’d like to show a project or talk through a question. Check the Luma event listing for anything specific to that meetup.

Zigbee? Z-Wave? Matter over Thread? Oh my.+

You don’t have to pick one for your whole home. Start with the device you need and check how it connects.

  • Zigbee: a mesh network for devices such as sensors, lights, and plugs. Home Assistant needs a supported Zigbee coordinator. Zigbee guide.
  • Z-Wave: another mesh network, using region-specific radio frequencies. You’ll need a supported Z-Wave adapter and devices for the same region. Z-Wave guide.
  • Thread: the low-power network that some smart home devices use. It needs a Thread border router to connect to your home network. Thread alone does not mean a device supports Matter.
  • Matter: the shared language a device uses to communicate with compatible controllers. A Matter device might use Thread, Wi-Fi, or Ethernet. “Matter over Thread” means Matter is communicating over a Thread network. Matter guide · Thread guide.

Already have a coordinator or border router? That’s a useful starting point. Check the exact device model and the Home Assistant documentation before buying. Bring your shortlist to Discord or a meetup and compare notes with people using it.

Is this an official Home Assistant group?+

We’re an independent, community-run group in Central Florida. We’re not affiliated with the Open Home Foundation.
